studies.title: Diagnosis and treatment of Wernicke's encephalopathy: A systematic literature review.
studies.abstract: Wernicke's encephalopathy (WE) is a serious neurological disorder that is underdiagnosed. Despite limited clinical guidelines, the standard use of intravenous (IV) thiamine is underutilized and remains an area of research deserving much attention. We conducted a systematic review using Medline, Embase, and CENTRAL databases to identify and summarize the literature on IV thiamine treatment in WE. Human studies with WE patients who received ≥100 mg of thiamine IV met inclusion criteria. Randomized controlled trials, cross-sectional studies, and case reports were included. A total of 27 studies were included: 20 case reports, five retrospective studies, one prospective study and one randomized control trial. Of the case reports, 11 (55%) cases were female, and the average age of all cases was 45 years (SD = 15). The other seven studies included 688 patients; the average age was 52 years (SD = 9), and 266 (38.7%) were female. Among the case reports, neurological and clinical findings were used to diagnose WE in 16 (80%) cases. MRI was utilized to diagnose 15 (75%) cases. 500 mg IV thiamine TID was reported in 12 case reports (60%). 18 (90%) of case reports had partial or complete resolution of symptoms following IV thiamine. IV thiamine can alleviate neurological symptoms, cognitive dysfunction, and brain imaging lesions associated with WE. We found key limitations in the evidence for IV thiamine and diagnostic standards for WE. Future targeted research should establish clear diagnostic and treatment guidelines for WE to prevent this serious condition from being underdiagnosed or undertreated.

studies.title: What is the optimum thiamine dose to treat or prevent Wernicke's encephalopathy or Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome? Results of a randomized controlled trial.
studies.abstract: The primary cause of Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome (WKS) is thiamine deficiency, and more than 90% of cases are reported in alcohol-dependent patients. While observational studies show parenteral thiamine administration drastically reduced WKS-related mortality, relevant treatment trials have never been conducted to determine the optimum thiamine dose. Two double-blind, parallel groups, randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were conducted to determine the optimal thiamine dose required for (1) the prevention of Wernicke's encephalopathy (WE), the acute phase of WKS, in asymptomatic but "at-risk" alcohol misuse patients (Study 1) and (2) the treatment of WE in symptomatic alcohol misuse patients (Study 2). Each study had a dosage regimen comprising three parenteral thiamine doses that were allocated at a ratio of 1:1:1. Study 1: Asymptomatic At-Risk patients (N = 393) received either 100 mg daily, 100 mg thrice daily, or 300 mg thrice daily, for 3 days. Study 2: Symptomatic patients (N = 127) received either 100 mg thrice daily, 300 mg thrice daily, or 500 mg thrice daily, for 5 days. Cognitive function was the primary outcome, assessed using the Rowland Universal Dementia Assessment Scale, two Cogstate subtests, and an adapted Story Memory Recall test. Secondary analyses examined differences in neurological function (ataxia, oculomotor abnormalities, and confusion) at follow-up. No significant differences were observed between any of the dosage conditions for either Study 1 or Study 2 on cognition or neurological functioning. This real-world study found that having a clinically unwell target population with high comorbidity and multiple presentations, coupled with challenges in cross-cultural assessment is likely to complicate RCT findings. The results of this study showed no clear benefit of high dose thiamine over intermediate or lower doses of thiamine, over the time intervals examined, for the treatment and prevention of cognitive and neurological abnormalities related to WKS. Several study limitations temper the interpretation of these findings. Nevertheless, the absence of conclusive evidence for the superiority of high-dose thiamine supports a recommendation for patient-specific treatment, while ensuring that the potential impact of other biochemical factors (e.g., magnesium and other B vitamin deficiencies) are considered and corrected if necessary.

studies.title: A pilot study of thiamin and folic acid in hemodialysis patients with cognitive impairment.
studies.abstract: This study aimed to explore the effectiveness of thiamin and folic acid supplementation on the improvement of the cognitive function in patients with maintenance hemodialysis. In the present study, we randomly assigned patients undergoing hemodialysis who had the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score lower than 26 to treatment group ( Patients in treatment group had an increase of the MoCA score from 21.95 ± 3.81 at baseline to 25.68 ± 1.96 at week 96 ( Hemodialysis patients with cognitive impairment treated with thiamin and folic acid had a significant improvement in MoCA score.

studies.title: Thiamine supplementation holds neurocognitive benefits for breastfed infants during the first year of life.
studies.abstract: Women reliant on mostly rice-based diets can have inadequate thiamine intake, placing breastfed infants at risk of thiamine deficiency and, in turn, physical and cognitive impairments. We investigated the impact of maternal thiamine supplementation doses on infants' cognitive, motor, and language development across the first year. In this double-blind, four-parallel-arm, randomized controlled trial, healthy mothers of exclusively breastfed newborn infants were recruited in Kampong Thom, Cambodia. At 2 weeks postnatal, women (n = 335) were randomized to one of four treatment groups to consume one capsule/day with varying amounts of thiamine for 22 weeks: 0, 1.2, 2.4, and 10 mg. At 2, 12, 24, and 52 weeks of age, infants were assessed with the Mullen Scales of Early Learning (MSEL) and the Caregiver Reported Early Development Instrument (CREDI). Multiple regression and mixed effects modeling suggest that by 6 months of age, the highest maternal thiamine dose (10 mg/day) held significant benefits for infants' language development, but generally not for motor or visual reception development. Despite having achieved standardized scores on the MSEL that approximated U.S. norms by 6 months, infants showed a significant drop relative to these norms in both language domains following trial completion, indicating that nutritional interventions beyond 6 months may be necessary.
studies.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences

studies.title: Thiamine supplementation in hospitalized patients with altered mental status: does it help?
studies.abstract: To describe thiamine-prescribing patterns and to study the association of thiamine supplementation with clinical outcomes in hospitalized patients with altered mental status (AMS). We conducted a retrospective cohort study of all adult hospitalized patients with AMS with index admission in calendar year 2017. We studied the association of a) supplemental thiamine and b) timing of thiamine relative to glucose, with hospital outcomes - length of stay (LOS), 90-day readmission rates, and mortality rates - using linear, logistic, and extended Cox models, respectively. We also modeled association of supplemental thiamine on time to resolution of AMS using extended Cox models in patients admitted with AMS. Of 985 patients, 178 (18%) received thiamine, including 123 (12.5%) who received thiamine before, with, or without glucose (thiamine first). We identified 365 (37%) patients who received intravenous glucose before or without thiamine (glucose first). We found that patients who received glucose first had longer LOS and higher rate of in-hospital deaths compared to those who did not. Patients who received thiamine supplementation had longer LOS compared to those who did not. There were no significant differences in other hospital outcomes or AMS resolution by discharge compared to their respective reference groups. Although thiamine supplementation was not associated with better hospital or cognitive outcomes, we do not have enough evidence to suggest a change in current practice. Thiamine must be administered prior to glucose in hospitalized patients with AMS.

studies.title: Ethnic differences in thiamine status persist after adjusting for diet; findings from the UK National Diet and Nutrition Survey.
studies.abstract:
Background/objectives

Thiamine (vitamin B1) status might play a role in cognition and mental health. Recent research suggests that there are ethnic differences in thiamine status. We aimed to test the hypothesis that black individuals have a higher risk of thiamine deficiency than white individuals, based on the erythrocyte transketolase activity coefficient (ETKAC), and assess differences in thiamine intake, using nutritional survey data.

Methods

We used the published data of the UK's National Diet and Nutrition Survey Rolling programme (2008-2019) and examined differences in the ETKAC between ethnicities and risk of thiamine deficiency (ETKAC >1.25). We also used dietary data to determine differences in thiamine intake between ethnic groups.

Results

Within the NDNS 2008-2019 ETKAC measurements were available for 5657 participants (5170 white, 92 black, 228 Asian, 93 mixed and 74 other ethnic groups). The median ETKAC of black participants was higher (1.15 (0.08) median (IQR)) than white (1.10 (0.07)) or Asian (1.12 (0.08)), indicating poorer thiamine status among black participants. The prevalence of thiamine deficiency was 5 % among black participants, being greater than among white (0.5 %) and Asian participants (1.3 %). This was independent of age, sex, body composition and socio-economic status. Dietary assessment data suggested that thiamine intake was on average lower for black participants compared to white or Asian participants Including dietary intake into the model was not sufficient to correct for the ethnic difference in thiamine status.

Conclusions

This study suggests that there are ethnic differences in thiamine status that cannot be readily explained by intake alone.

studies.abstract: The relationship between thiamine blood level (TBL) and cognition remains uncertain, including among alcohol-dependent persons (ADP). To evaluate this relationship during protocol-driven inpatient alcohol detoxification treatment including thiamine supplementation (AD + Th). Prospective 3-week study with 100 consecutively admitted detoxification-seeking ADP (47.7 ± 11 years old, 21% females) without superseding comorbidities requiring treatment. TBL and Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) were measured at admission (t We found no cases of Wernicke Encephalopathy (WE) and only one case of thiamine deficiency. Both MoCA and TBL significantly improved across AD + Th (with medium-to-large effect sizes). At t TBL was a robust predictor of pre-detoxification cognitive impairment, and both TBL and cognition improved significantly during AD + Th (including abstinence) in our ADP population, supporting routine thiamine supplementation for ADP, even those at low WE-risk. The TBL-cognition relationship was minimally confounded by age, alcohol-toxicity proxies, mood, and vitamin D levels.

studies.title: Vitamin B1 protects against Aβ<sub>1-42</sub>-induced HIF-1α activation and neurotoxicity.
studies.abstract: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by cognitive decline and extensive neuronal loss, largely driven by amyloid beta (Aβ) accumulation and associated cellular stress. Vitamin B1 (thiamine) supplementation has demonstrated cognitive benefits in clinical AD studies, however, the mechanisms underlying thiamine's neuroprotective effects remain unclear. Here, we investigated whether thiamine mitigates Aβ<sub>1-42</sub>-induced neurotoxicity by suppressing hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha (HIF-1α), a transcriptional stress factor regulating many proapoptotic and progressive amyloidogenic pathways. Exposure of neuronal cells to Aβ<sub>1-42</sub> oligomers increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, decreased intracellular Fe<sup>2+</sup>, and induced HIF-1α stabilization. HIF-1α activation by Aβ<sub>1-42</sub> promoted apoptosis through increased endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and increased mitochondrial dimerization of BNIP3. Thiamine supplementation significantly reduced cellular ROS levels, preserved intracellular Fe<sup>2+</sup> levels, and restored prolyl hydroxylase (PHD) activity to promote HIF-1α hydroxylation and degradation. Suppression of HIF-1α by thiamine attenuated ER and BNIP3-driven apoptotic pathways and preserved neuronal viability. Thiamine further mitigated HIF-1α-mediated amyloidogenic progression, limiting feedback toxicity caused by Aβ<sub>1-42</sub>. These results demonstrate that thiamine protects against Aβ<sub>1-42</sub>-mediated neurotoxicity by reducing ROS, preserving Fe<sup>2+</sup>, and inhibiting HIF-1α-driven pathological cascades. Overall, this study identified a novel mechanism for thiamine's neuroprotective role, further supporting its therapeutic potential to limit neurodegenerative progression in AD.

studies.title: Does thiamine supplementation affect heart failure? A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized control trials.
studies.abstract: Heart failure is a pathophysiological condition where decreased cardiac output is observed subsequent to any structural deformity or cessation of normal function. Thiamine deficiency is one of the risk factors responsible for causing HF; other risk factors include hypertension, smoking, and obesity. We conducted a systemic review and meta-analysis of RCTs to scrutinize whether the heart failure patients would benefit from thiamine supplementation or not when compared to placebo. We selected only those double-arm randomized controlled trials (RCTs) which included participants presenting with symptomatic heart failure. We excluded all the articles published in languages other than English Language. Furthermore, all the studies other than RCTs were also omitted. Articles yielded from the electronic search were exported to EndNote Reference Library software to remove any duplicates. Analyses were done using the Review manager 5.4 tool. Mean values and standard deviations were retrieved for the continuous outcomes given as raw data. The 6 RCTs selected for the statistical analysis consisted of 298 participants (158 in the intervention group, 140 in the placebo group). The outcomes resulted to be non-significant with LVEF p-value= 0.08, NT-pro BNP p-value= 0.94, LVEDV p-value= 0.53, 6MWT p-value=0.59, mortality p-value= 0.61, hospitalization p-value= 0.53 and dyspnea p-value= 0.77. Heart rate is the only significant outcome with a p-value=0.04. To conclude, except for heart rate, thiamine supplementation had no effect on the outcomes of heart failure patients.

studies.title: Sustained High-dose Thiamine Supplementation in High-risk Cardiac Patients Undergoing Cardiopulmonary Bypass: A Pilot Feasibility Study (The APPLY trial).
studies.abstract: To test the feasibility and investigate possible cardiovascular effects of a sustained high-dose intravenous thiamine protocol in patients undergoing combined valvular and coronary artery bypass graft surgery. Randomized, placebo-controlled, pilot feasibility trial. Cardiac surgery department of a tertiary hospital. Forty patients undergoing combined valvular and coronary artery bypass surgery. Intravenous thiamine (600 mg on the day of surgery, and 400 mg/day on postoperative days 1, 2, and 3) or placebo. The primary feasibility endpoints were recruitment rate and protocol compliance. Secondary endpoints included markers of possible biological and physiological effects. The mean recruitment rate was 8 patients per month and protocol compliance was 97.5%. There were no differences in median peak postoperative lactate (2.7 mmol/L [interquartile range [IQR] 1.4-4.6] for thiamine v 2.5 mmol/L [IQR 1.4-3.6] for placebo; p = 0.53), median peak postoperative creatinine (104 µmol/L [IQR 92.5-129] for thiamine v 99 µmol/L [IQR 86.5-109.5] for placebo; p = 0.53), median nadir postoperative cardiac index (1.8 L/min/m A double-blind trial of sustained high-dose intravenous thiamine supplementation in higher-risk cardiac surgery patients was feasible and appeared to be safe. However, such treatment did not demonstrate evidence of biological or physiological effects.

studies.title: Physiological and performance responses to supplementation with thiamin and pantothenic acid derivatives.
studies.abstract: The purpose of this study was to investigate the physiological and performance responses to supplementation with allithiamin and pantethine. On two separate occasions, six highly trained cyclists [maximum O2 consumption or VO2max 61.8 (2.1) ml x kg(-1) x min(-1)] performed a 50-km steady-state ride on a cycle ergometer at a workload corresponding to approximately 60% of VO2max followed by a 2000-m time trial. For 7 days prior to each ride, subjects daily ingested either a placebo (PL) or a combination of 1 g of allithiamin and 1.8 g of a 55%/45% pantethine/pantothenic acid compound (AP). Treatments were administered using a randomized, double-blind, counter-balanced design. During the 50km ride, measures of heart rate, respiratory gas exchange and ratings of perceived exertion were recorded at 5, 15, 25, 35 and 45 km. Blood samples were collected at 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 km and analyzed for lactate, glucose and free fatty acids. Blood samples for the analysis of lactate were also collected 3 and 5 min after the completion of the 2000-m time trial. There were no significant differences in any of the measured parameters between experimental conditions. Time to complete the 2000-m time trial was also not significantly different between experimental conditions [PL 178.2 (8.4), AP 170.7 (10.2) s; P=0.58]. These results suggest that, despite the reported enhanced absorption properties, supplementation with allithiamin and pantethine does not alter exercise metabolism or exercise performance.

studies.title: The response to treatment of subclinical thiamine deficiency in the elderly.
studies.abstract: The significance of subclinical thiamine deficiency in the elderly was determined by assessing response to thiamine supplementation in a randomized double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. Thirty-five of 222 people aged > or = 65 y had two concentrations of erythrocyte thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) < 140 nmol/L 3 mo apart and 41 other people had the first, but not the second, TPP concentration below this value. Both groups were randomly assigned in a double-blind trial to oral thiamine (10 mg/d) or a placebo. All subjects randomly assigned to receive thiamine showed increases in TPP concentrations compared with control subjects. Only the subjects with persistently low TPP concentrations showed subjective benefits from treatment with improvements in quality of life (measured on a visual analogue scale; P = 0.02) and decreases in systolic blood pressure (P = 0.05) and weight (P < 0.01) when compared with subjects given placebo. There was a trend toward benefits in sleep and energy (P = 0.07). We conclude that a low TPP concentration on two occasions is a better predictor of response to treatment than an isolated measurement. Quality of life was enhanced by providing thiamine supplements. Blood pressure and weight were lower after thiamine supplementation.

studies.title: Gastrointestinal Beriberi Secondary to Intermittent Hemodialysis With Rapid Improvement Following Thiamine Administration.
studies.abstract: Thiamine deficiency is classically linked to malnutrition and chronic alcohol use, but emerging evidence indicates that patients on intermittent hemodialysis (iHD) are also at significant risk. While cardiovascular and neurologic syndromes are well characterized, gastrointestinal (GI) beriberi remains an underrecognized presentation. We describe a 67-year-old man on iHD with chronic abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and anorexia refractory to conventional therapy. Workup revealed elevated lactate and a low plasma thiamine level prior to supplementation. Symptoms and elevated lactate resolved rapidly following intravenous thiamine. This case underscores GI beriberi as a treatable cause of chronic GI symptoms in dialysis patients.

studies.title: The relationship between dietary vitamin B1 and stroke: a machine learning analysis of NHANES data.
studies.abstract:
Background

Vitamin B1 deficiency is closely linked to damage in the cardiovascular system. However, the relationship between dietary Vitamin B1 intake and the risk of stroke remains ambiguous and requires further investigation.

Methods

This study analyzed data from participants in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES: 2005-2018) to investigate the relationship between dietary vitamin B1 and ischemic stroke. Weighted multivariable logistic regression models and restricted cubic spline (RCS) regression were employed to explore potential nonlinear relationships, and subgroup analyses were conducted to assess the robustness of the results. Additionally, the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) was utilized for feature selection. Eight machine learning methods were employed to construct predictive models and evaluate their performance. Based on the best-performing model, we further examined variable importance and model accuracy, employing Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis to interpret the model. Finally, a nomogram was created to enhance the readability of the predictive model results.

Results

After controlling for various variables, vitamin B1 exhibited a significant linear negative correlation with stroke risk. In comparison to the lowest quartile, the adjusted odds ratio (OR) for the fourth quartile was notably reduced to 0.66 (95% CI: 0.46, 0.94). Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis further confirmed a linear inverse relationship between vitamin B1 levels and stroke risk. Moreover, the Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM) model demonstrated robust predictive efficacy, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 91.9%.

Conclusion

A large-scale study based on NHANES indicates that as dietary intake of vitamin B1 increases, the risk of stroke shows a gradual decline. Therefore, appropriately increasing dietary intake of vitamin B1 may reduce the risk of stroke occurrence.

studies.title: Thiamine supplementation differentially enhances stress tolerance and high-value product accumulation in Chromochloris zofingiensis under nitrogen deficiency an
studies.abstract: Microalgae are promising feedstocks for the production of high-value compounds such as lipids and carotenoids, owing to their rapid growth and metabolic flexibility. Abiotic stresses are widely used to enhance the accumulation of high-value metabolites in microalgae, but they often inhibit cell growth and ultimately reduce overall yield. Functioning as an essential cofactor, thiamine (Vitamin B1) has been demonstrated to significantly enhance cellular stress resistance. Therefore, the effects of exogenous thiamine supplementation on astaxanthin and total fatty acid (TFA) accumulation were assessed in Chromochloris zofingiensis under nitrogen deprivation (ND) and high salinity (HS) conditions. Results showed that thiamine supplementation significantly enhanced cell proliferation and growth, with the highest increases in dry weight (DW) reaching 63.29 % under ND and 49.53 % under HS at a concentration of 0.5 mg/L. Thiamine also reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels by 40.03 % under ND and 62.2 % under HS. Additionally, under ND, thiamine promoted the accumulation of astaxanthin and TFA, and lead to a 200 % increase in astaxanthin yield and a 51.12 % increase in TFA yield. Whereas under HS, thiamine supplementation had no significant effect on astaxanthin and TFA accumulation, it enhanced astaxanthin yield by 56 % at 0.5 mg/L, primarily due to its growth-promoting effect. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses showed that thiamine supplementation upregulated the glycolysis and gluconeogenesis pathways, pyruvate metabolism, starch and sucrose metabolism, and fatty acid biosynthesis pathways, thereby redirecting carbon flux toward lipid and carotenoid biosynthesis. In contrast, under HS, it activated pathways related to alpha-linolenic acid metabolism, linoleic acid metabolism, and arginine and proline metabolism, which contributed to osmotic regulation and antioxidant capacity. This study elucidated the differential regulatory mechanisms of thiamine in C. zofingiensis under ND and HS conditions, highlighting its potential as an effective strategy for enhancing stress tolerance and boosting astaxanthin and TFA production in microalgae.

studies.title: Effects of dietary thiamin (vitamin B1) on the growth performance, serum biochemical factors, immune response, and antioxidant activity of great sturgeon (Huso
studies.abstract: The present research evaluated the positive effects of dietary thiamin (vitamin B1) levels on the growth performance, serum biochemistry factors, immune response, and antioxidant activity of great sturgeon (Huso huso) juveniles. Thiamin was included in diets with levels of 0 (control, T0), 7 (T7), 15 (T15), and 25 (T25) mg/kg diet. Measurements of thiamin levels in diets indicated that they contained 1.80 (T0), 8.02 (T7), 16.2 (T15), and 26.6 (T25) mg thiamin/kg feed. Sturgeon juveniles (240 individuals) with average weight of 44.8 ± 1.96 g were distributed into 12 tanks, and fed with the experimental diets for 8 weeks. Final weight, body weight gain (%), specific growth rate, and feed conversion ratio (FCR) of great sturgeon were significantly influenced by dietary thiamin levels, and the maximum fish performance (P < 0.05) was obtained at a level of 15 mg/kg diet. The trypsin, chymotrypsin, creatine kinase, lipase, α-amylase, and alkaline phosphatase activities were notably (P < 0.05) affected by the dietary thiamin levels. The glucose content was not significantly (P > 0.05) different among the experimental treatments. Diets supplemented with thiamine increased significantly (P < 0.05) triglyceride, cholesterol, and total protein levels accompanied with significant (P < 0.05) decreases in aminotransferase aspartate and alanine aminotransferase activities. Serum antioxidant enzymes were remarkably (P < 0.05) higher, while serum malondialdehyde was significantly (P < 0.05) lower in the thiamin-treated fish compared with the control group. Total immunoglobulin, lysozyme, and ACH50 values were significantly (P < 0.05) higher in fish fed with thiamin-supplemented diets than in the control group. The results of the present study demonstrated that dietary thiamin have an important role in enhancing the growth performance, immune response, and antioxidant activity of great sturgeon. Based on the regression fitting curve of final weight, weight gain, specific growth rate, and FCR values, the optimal level of thiamin is found to be 15.0-17.5 mg/kg diet.

studies.title: Effect of Supplementation of Vitamin C and Thiamine on the Outcome in Sepsis: South East Asian Region.
studies.abstract: The global burden of sepsis is overwhelming and novel therapeutic agents is the need of the hour. The present study was designed to understand the role of Malondialdehyde as a marker of the oxidative stress in sepsis, as well as the effect of supplementation of Vitamin C and Thiamine in patients of sepsis. 80 patients of sepsis were randomly divided into 4 groups of 20 each. Twenty age-sex matched healthy volunteers were chosen as controls. The first group received Vitamin C, the second group received Thiamine, the third group received both and the fourth group received neither. Vitamin C (2g 8 hourly) and Thiamine (200 mg 12 hourly) were given intravenously for five days. The outcome was recorded in terms of mortality in the various groups as well as by the improvement in SOFA scores (ΔSOFA). The serum levels of Vitamin C, Thiamine and Malondialdehyde were estimated. Among the 80 patients, 17 (21%) were in septic shock. The mortality rate was 10% overall, and 47% among patients of septic shock. No additional mortality benefit was observed in the groups supplemented with Vitamin C and Thiamine. However, the ΔSOFA score in patients who received both Vitamin C and Thiamine was significantly higher as compared to the other groups. The mean malondialdehyde level was higher in patients of sepsis (1.81±1.18 µmol/l) as compared with healthy controls (0.78 ± 0.36 µmol/l). The Vitamin C level and Thiamine level (estimated indirectly by TPP effect), at presentation were 5.14±4.19 ng/ml and 52.99±28.45 % in patients of sepsis, which was significantly lower than that in healthy controls, in whom the levels were 14.64±5.51 ng/ml and 27.55±13.67% respectively. Vitamin C and Thiamine supplementation is a cost-effective approach with a good safety profile. Additional studies including a larger population is required to study the mortality benefits and reaffirm our findings.

studies.title: Randomised clinical trial: high-dose oral thiamine versus placebo for chronic fatigue in patients with quiescent inflammatory bowel disease.
studies.abstract: Fatigue is a burdensome symptom for patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Few pharmacological interventions have documented effect on fatigue in patients with IBD. A pilot study indicated a 20-day effect  with high-dose thiamine. To investigate the effect and safety of high-dose oral thiamine (600-1800 mg/d) based on gender and weight on chronic fatigue in patients with quiescent IBD. This was a randomised, double-blinded, placebo-controlled crossover trial. Patients had quiescent IBD, severe chronic fatigue and no other explanation for fatigue. Patients were allocated 1:1 to either 1) high-dose oral thiamine for 4 weeks, 4 weeks of washout, 4 weeks of oral placebo or 2) oral placebo for 4 weeks, 4 weeks of washout, 4 weeks of high-dose oral thiamine. Fatigue was measured using the Inflammatory Bowel Disease-Fatigue Questionnaire. The primary outcome was improvement (≥3 points) of fatigue after 4 weeks on thiamine. Forty patients were enrolled between November 2018 and October 2019. Crossover analysis showed a mean reduction of 4.5 points (95% CI 2.6-6.2) in fatigue after thiamine compared with a mean increase of 0.75 point (95% CI -1.3-2.8; P = 0.0003) after placebo. Furthermore, 55% of group 1 and 75% of group 2 showed an improvement ≥ 3 points while on thiamine compared with 25% of group 1 and 35% of group 2 while on placebo. Only mild side effects were detected. We showed a significant beneficial effect of high-dose oral thiamine on chronic fatigue in IBD. The treatment was well tolerated. NCT03634735.

studies.title: L-shaped association of vitamin B1 with pelvic inflammatory disease: A cross-sectional study.
studies.abstract: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) is a common gynecological condition. While vitamin intake may influence PID risk, the role of vitamin B1 remains unclear. This cross-sectional study explored the association between vitamin B1 intake and PID risk. This study included data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2013 to 2018. Weighted multivariate logistic regression, subgroup analyses, smooth curve fitting, and threshold effect modeling were applied in this study. A total of 3954 women aged 20 to 59 years were included. Tertile analysis confirmed a dose-response relationship: compared with the lowest tertile (Q1), both middle (Q2) and highest (Q3) tertiles showed reduced PID risk, with Q3 exhibiting the strongest protective effect (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 0.631, P = .006). We identified an L-shaped association between vitamin B1 and PID. A significant negative correlation was observed when vitamin B1 intake was <1.938 (OR = 0.575, 95% confidence interval = 0.417-0.793, P < .001), whereas no statistically significant association was detected when intake exceeded 1.938 (OR = 1.370, 95% confidence interval = 0.769-2.440, P = .285). Subgroup analysis showed the association differed by hypertension, diabetes, and nonvigorous physical activity subgroups. The relationship between vitamin B1 intake and PID conformed to an L-shaped curve (nonlinear, P = .009), with the inflection point measured at 1.938 mg/d, highlighting the close association between nutritional status and gynecological health. These results suggest that vitamin B1 may correlate with a lower risk of PID. Further prospective studies are needed to explore the underlying mechanisms.

studies.title: Case Report: A rare case of concurrent diabetic ketoacidosis and severe acute pancreatitis, followed by Guillain-Barré syndrome and Wernicke's encephalopathy.
studies.abstract: The coexistence of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) and severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) is a life-threatening metabolic emergency complicated by multiple organ dysfunction syndrome. The sequential development of Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) and Wernicke's encephalopathy (WE) in such critically ill patients is exceedingly rare and prone to missed diagnosis. A 26-year-old obese male was admitted with unconsciousness after excessive cola ingestion. He was diagnosed with DKA, SAP, pneumonia, sepsis. During hospitalization, the patient developed progressive visual impairment, dysphagia, hoarseness, and ophthalmoplegia. Neurological examination revealed diminished to absent tendon reflexes. Typical albumin-cytologic dissociation was detected in cerebrospinal fluid. Cranial magnetic resonance imaging showed characteristic hyperintense signals in the mammillary bodies and periaqueductal region, accompanied by reduced serum vitamin B1 levels, consistent with WE. The patient was eventually diagnosed with overlapping GBS and WE. He received repeated intravenous immunoglobulin therapy and thiamine supplementation. The patient's neurological function gradually recovered and he was discharged in stable condition. Critical illness-related systemic inflammation, metabolic derangements and infection can induce GBS, while inadequate thiamine supplementation and heightened consumption result in severe thiamine deficiency complicated by WE. Close neurological monitoring, timely thiamine supplementation, and standardized immunotherapy contribute to favorable clinical outcomes.

studies.title: Dietary thiamine supplementation enhances the growth performance, digestive enzyme activity, intestine development, immunity and anti-inflammatory gene expressi
studies.abstract: This research aimed to determine the dietary requirement of thiamine and evaluate its effects on olive flounder (Paralichthys olivaceus). Control diet (Con) was formulated without thiamine supplementation, while four additional diets were formulated with thiamine concentrations of 4, 8, 12 and 16 mg/kg diet (designated as T4, T8, T12 and T16, respectively). A total of 300 fish (initial weight, 55.5 ± 1.3 g) were randomly distributed into 15 tanks (triplicate groups per treatment, 20 fish per tank) and fed for 10 weeks. One-way ANOVA was performed to analyze treatment effects. Final body weight was significantly increased in all the thiamine-supplemented groups compared to the Con group. Significant improvements in weight gain, specific growth rate and feed utilization were observed in T4 and T16 groups compared to the Con group. Immune responses, including anti-protease, lysozyme and myeloperoxidase activities and total immnunoglobulin concentration were significantly increased in the T4-T12 thiamine-supplemented groups. Antioxidant activity was significantly increased in all thiamine-supplemented groups. Trypsin activity was significantly elevated in the 4-12 mg/kg groups, while amylase and lipase activities were enhanced in all thiamine-supplemented groups. Anti-inflammatory genes were significantly upregulated in thiamine-supplemented groups compared to the Con. Thiamine supplementation promoted an increase in goblet cell count and villi length in intestine. A broken-line regression analysis for weight gain indicated that the optimal thiamine requirement for olive flounder would be 3.05 mg/kg diet. These findings demonstrate the positive effects of dietary thiamine on growth, immunity, antioxidant activity, digestive enzyme activity and intestinal health in olive flounder.

studies.title: Thiamine (Vitamin B1) metabolism in schistosomes.
studies.abstract: Schistosomes are intravascular parasitic flatworms that acquire all nutrients necessary for their survival from blood. Here we focus on how the parasites acquire and metabolize an essential nutrient - vitamin B1 (thiamine). Live adult male and female Schistosoma mansoni parasites cleave exogenous thiamine monophosphate (ThMP) and thiamine pyrophosphate (ThPP) to generate free thiamine. Of the three characterized nucleotide-metabolizing ectoenzymes expressed at the schistosome surface (SmAP, SmNPP5, and SmATPDase1), only SmAP hydrolyzes these metabolites. Parasites whose SmAP gene is suppressed by RNAi are significantly impaired in their ability to cleave ThMP, but not ThPP, compared to controls. We conclude therefore that while SmAP can cleave ThMP alone, additional (uncharacterized) ectoenzyme(s) also cleave ThPP. When schistosomes are incubated in murine plasma, levels of both thiamine and phosphate increase over time, a finding consistent with these data. Generating a pool of free thiamine around the worms should permit the convenient uptake of this vital metabolite. However, we were unable to identify homologs in schistosomes of thiamine transporter proteins described in other systems. Instead, a ThPP transporter homolog was identified in silico (SmThPPT). Additionally, a schistosome mitochondrial ThPP transporter homolog is described that likely moves some imported ThPP from the cytoplasm into worm mitochondria. Finally, we report on a thiamine pyrophosphokinase homolog (SmTPK) that could pyrophosphorylate thiamine to make ThPP. Free thiamine generated outside the worms, if not imported (and since it is anti-inflammatory), could act in an immunomodulatory capacity to help generate a more benign external environment for the worms in the bloodstream.

studies.title: Chronic oxidative stress leads to the accumulation of reversibly oxidised thiamine derivatives in tissues: effects of thiamine and cholecalciferol.
studies.abstract: There is limited data on oxidised thiamine (vitamin B<sub>1</sub>) derivatives in animal and human tissues. Some studies suggest that oxidative stress (OS) leads to their formation. This study aimed to estimate the proportion of reversibly oxidised (disulfide) thiamine derivatives in the total vitamin B<sub>1</sub> pool in rat tissues exposed to various chronic OS forms, and to investigate the possibility of reducing these derivatives to a cyclic form. Rat models of thiamine deficiency and chronic alcoholism were used in experiments. The thiochrome method was used to analyse thiamine, with pretreatment of samples with a reducing agent and hydrolysis of thiamine phosphates performed separately under optimal conditions. The analysis of active and oxidised forms of vitamin B<sub>1</sub>, standard markers of OS and blood levels of 25(OH)D<sub>3</sub> was performed in tissue samples. The corrective effect of thiamine and vitamin D<sub>3</sub> supplementation was studied. In both models of OS, there was a decrease in the proportion of the active (cyclic) form of thiamine and a sharp increase in its oxidised (disulfide) forms, reaching levels of ∼50-70% of the total thiamine pool. High doses of thiamine (2 mg/kg) or vitamin D<sub>3</sub> (2000 IU/kg) completely or partially normalized the situation with regard to OS indicators and also reduced the proportion of oxidised thiamine. Our results show that OS causes thiamine deficiency and tissue accumulation of thiamine disulfide derivatives. Red blood cell thiamine disulfide levels serve as a reliable marker of chronic OS, whereas a positive vitamin D deficiency test can mask actual vitamin B<sub>1</sub> deficiency.

studies.title: Thiamine Mitigates Nicotine Withdrawal Effects in Adolescent Male Rats: Modulation of Serotonin Metabolism, BDNF, Oxidative Stress, and Neuroinflammation.
studies.abstract: Adolescent nicotine use is particularly concerning due to increased susceptibility to long-term effects and dependence during this critical developmental period. This study investigates the therapeutic effects of thiamine on nicotine withdrawal-induced anxiety, anhedonia, and depression in rats. Adolescent rats received nicotine (2 mg/kg, s.c.) for 21 d, followed by 21 d of withdrawal. Thiamine (25 or 50 mg/kg, i.p.) was administered during exposure and withdrawal. Behavioral assessments were used to evaluate anxiety- and depressive-like symptoms, and biochemical analyses measured oxidative stress markers, serotonin levels, MAO activity, BDNF, and GFAP as indicators of neuroinflammation in the prefrontal cortex. Nicotine withdrawal significantly elevated anxiety-, depression-, and anhedonia-like behaviors, increased oxidative stress, and upregulated MAO-A activity and GFAP expression, indicating neuroinflammatory effects. Notably, thiamine administration during both nicotine exposure and withdrawal effectively alleviated these behavioral impairments, restored serotonin levels, reduced oxidative stress markers, and mitigated the increase in GFAP expression. Additionally, thiamine alone has been shown to alleviate anxiety- and depressive-like behaviors. This study highlights thiamine's potential as a promising intervention for managing psychological distress associated with nicotine withdrawal. Given the high prevalence of adolescent nicotine use and its associated mental health challenges, further research on thiamine's mechanisms and therapeutic potential is warranted to improve treatment strategies during this critical developmental stage.

studies.title: Thiamine ameliorates inflammation of the ruminal epithelium of Saanen goats suffering from subacute ruminal acidosis.

explanation.what_it_is_line: Essential B vitamin your body uses to unlock energy from food; corrects deficiency diseases.
explanation.what_it_is: Thiamine, also called vitamin B1, is a water-soluble vitamin your cells need to convert food (carbohydrates and certain amino acids) into usable energy. Your body cannot make it; you must get it from food or supplements. It's found naturally in whole grains, pork, legumes, and nuts. People typically take it as an oral tablet or capsule, or receive it by injection—the injectable form is especially used in medical settings to treat or prevent severe deficiency.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Converts into a coenzyme that enables enzymes to release energy; supports nerve and heart function.
explanation.how_it_works: Thiamine is converted inside your cells into thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP), a helper molecule (called a coenzyme) that works like a key fitting into an enzyme lock. Without it, several critical enzymes cannot function—specifically those that release energy from carbohydrates and help build and repair nerve tissue and cell membranes. This is why thiamine deficiency damages the nervous system and heart first: those tissues depend heavily on stable energy supply. TPP also plays a role in managing inflammation-related signaling, though the full picture of how it does so is still being researched. Your brain, heart, and muscles are especially sensitive to thiamine shortage because they burn energy constantly.
explanation.safety_line: Short-term oral and injected use well-tolerated; long-term safety and drug interactions incompletely studied.
explanation.safety_detail: The retrieved trials report few adverse events in short-term oral and intravenous thiamine supplementation, even at high doses. However, most published studies enrolled adults over days to weeks; long-term safety in the general population, effects in children outside hospital settings, and interactions with other medications are not well characterized in the records provided.
safety_bullets: Pregnancy and lactation: thiamine is essential during these periods, but optimal dosing and safety of high-dose supplementation in pregnant/nursing people is not addressed in the retrieved studies.
Kidney disease and dialysis: some retrieved studies enrolled dialysis patients, but dosing safety in severe renal impairment remains incompletely defined.
Drug interactions: no retrieved trial examined thiamine interactions with major drug classes; unknown in clinical practice.
Long-term high-dose use: almost all retrieved studies used supplementation for days to weeks; effects of years of high-dose oral thiamine are not documented in the records provided.
explanation.chem_meaning: Thiamine is a polar, water-loving molecule (XLogP 1 indicates it dissolves well in water and is absorbed from the small intestine) with a positively charged thiazolium ring. This charge and polarity make it readily absorbed orally but also mean it does not accumulate in fat tissue, so the body excretes excess amounts daily—deficiency can develop quickly if intake is cut off.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Multiple meta-analyses and systematic reviews converge on the finding that thiamine supplementation corrects and prevents beriberi (a disease causing heart failure, nerve damage, and death from thiamine deficiency). Across studies enrolling over 23,000 verified participants—including critically ill patients, dialysis patients, and populations at high risk of deficiency—thiamine administration (oral and intravenous, at various doses) reverses deficiency symptoms and reduces mortality when deficiency is present. A 2024 systematic review of 688 people examined diagnosis and treatment of Wernicke's encephalopathy (the acute neurologic form of severe deficiency); a 2026 RCT of 2,784 septic patients showed thiamine use was associated with mortality reduction. The evidence spans recent years (2021–2026) and includes adequately powered trials.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Strong grade reflects 52 human studies with independent replication across 4 meta-analyses, consistency of effect direction, and over 23,000 verified participants in the outcome. Thiamine supplementation for established deficiency is not controversial—this is standard medical practice supported by robust synthesis.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Thiamine supplementation is effective for treating and preventing Wernicke encephalopathy, an acute neurologic emergency (confusion, eye movement abnormalities, ataxia—loss of coordination) caused by severe thiamine deficiency. A 2024 systematic review (n=688) examined diagnosis and treatment; a 2022 RCT (n=393) investigated optimal thiamine dosing to prevent and treat Wernicke–Korsakoff syndrome (the chronic form). Over 16,000 verified participants across 17 of 44 studies demonstrate that prompt thiamine administration, especially intravenously, halts progression and reverses early symptoms. Three independent meta-analyses/systematic reviews converge on efficacy.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Strong grade: 35 human studies, 3 independent syntheses confirming outcome, ~16,000 verified participants, and clear clinical benefit in reversing a life-threatening neurologic emergency. Thiamine is the standard first-line treatment for suspected Wernicke encephalopathy in medicine.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: A 2021 RCT pilot study in hemodialysis patients with cognitive impairment, a 2021 RCT (n=335) of thiamine supplementation in breastfed infants during the first year of life, and a 2022 observational study (n=985) of hospitalized patients with altered mental status suggest thiamine may support cognitive function and mental status recovery. A 2022 RCT (n=393) on optimal dosing for Wernicke's encephalopathy also assessed cognitive outcomes. However, only one meta-analysis/systematic review is documented in the records, and its conclusions have not been independently replicated.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderate grade: 7 human studies exist with some evidence of cognitive benefit, but only a single synthesis review; no independent replication of pooled findings. Studies span pilot designs and observational work, which are less definitive than multiple large RCTs. The outcome is plausible—thiamine is critical for neurotransmitter synthesis and energy metabolism in the brain—but clinical evidence remains preliminary.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: A 2023 meta-analysis (n=298) examined whether thiamine supplementation affects heart failure; a 2020 RCT investigated sustained high-dose thiamine in high-risk cardiac patients undergoing cardiopulmonary bypass; older RCTs (1997–1998) studied thiamine's effects on cardiac performance and exercise response. A 2026 case report described rapid improvement in gastrointestinal beriberi (a cardiac-related emergency) after thiamine administration. About 538 verified participants are documented across 2 of 8 studies; most abstracts lack sample sizes, so the true total may be larger. However, only one meta-analysis appears in the records, and its conclusion is not independently verified.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderate grade: 6 human studies with mechanistic plausibility (thiamine is essential for heart muscle energy production) but only one synthesis and no independent replication. Studies are small to moderate in size and span decades; recent, large, adequately powered RCTs specifically on cardiac outcomes appear limited in the records provided. Evidence for thiamine in established heart disease is suggestive but not definitive.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: A 2022 RCT (n=60) in gestational diabetes found anti-inflammatory and antioxidative effects of thiamine supplements; a 2022 RCT (n=80) examining vitamin C and thiamine combination in sepsis; a 2021 RCT in chronic fatigue patients; and a 2026 observational study (n=3,954) reporting an L-shaped association between vitamin B1 and pelvic inflammatory disease. Animal studies (n=300) showed dietary thiamine enhanced digestive enzyme activity and intestinal development. About 4,394 participants are verified across 4 of 10 studies; most other abstracts omit size. However, no pooled analysis confirms the multiple studies agree; consistency is not yet established.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderate grade: 5 human and 5 animal studies suggest anti-inflammatory potential, but no meta-analysis has synthesized them, and the studies are somewhat heterogeneous in design and populations (gestational diabetes, sepsis, chronic fatigue, pelvic disease). The mechanistic role of thiamine's TPP form in inflammatory signaling is plausible but incompletely understood. Evidence is suggestive and warrants further synthesis but falls short of Strong.

explanation.evidence_base: Thiamine deficiency and Wernicke encephalopathy have Strong evidence (52 and 35 human studies respectively, with multiple meta-analyses) and represent well-established clinical applications. Cognition, cardiovascular, and inflammation outcomes are Moderate grade and rely on 5–7 human studies per outcome with limited pooled analysis. The literature is dominated by human trials (mostly RCTs and systematic reviews from 2020–2026, with some older work), reflecting decades of clinical use and recent renewed focus on thiamine in critical illness and neurologic disease. Animal studies support mechanism but are fewer and not the basis of the clinical grades.
explanation.open_questions: The retrieved records show strong evidence for deficiency correction and Wernicke encephalopathy but limited data on cognition, cardiovascular, and inflammation in non-deficient or mildly deficient populations—it is unclear whether supplementation in people with normal thiamine status confers benefit. Long-term safety and optimal dosing outside acute hospital settings are not well characterized. Outcome-specific gaps: cognition studies include infants and elderly but lack mid-life populations; cardiovascular studies are small and old (except one 2020 trial); inflammation work spans only 5 human trials without synthesis. Note: these gaps reflect what is visible in the ~40 abstracts provided per outcome; the full literature may be broader, but we cannot assess that here.

appraisal.headline: The evidence base is genuinely strong for thiamine deficiency and Wernicke encephalopathy (with 4 independent meta-analyses and ~16k–24k verified participants), but weaker outcomes (cognition, cardiovascular, inflammation) rely on single syntheses, small studies, and designs that often omit sample sizes, limiting confidence in those claims.

concerns.issue: Sample size reporting opaque for weaker outcomes
concerns.detail: For cognition, cardiovascular, and inflammation outcomes, only 5–38% of studies report sample sizes in their abstracts. The engine notes 'most abstracts omit sample size,' meaning true N is unknown. For cardiovascular, only 2 of 8 studies report N (298, 240); for inflammation, only 4 of 10 report N. This opacity makes it impossible to assess whether these outcomes rest on adequate precision or are driven by a small number of large trials—a critical distinction for Moderate-graded claims.

concerns.issue: Single synthesis only for cognition and cardiovascular
concerns.detail: Both cognition and cardiovascular outcomes are graded Moderate precisely because 'a single meta-analysis / systematic review exists, but its conclusion is not independently replicated or verified.' For cardiovascular, only one 2023 meta-analysis (n=298) is listed. If that synthesis contains bias or methodological issues, there is no second independent synthesis to validate or contradict it. This is a fundamental limitation the engine itself flagged.

concerns.issue: Inflammation evidence lacks pooled synthesis and consistency confirmation
concerns.detail: The engine explicitly notes 'several studies exist but no pooled analysis confirms they agree; held at moderate pending review.' The 10 studies span animal and human designs; the 5 human studies include only 3 RCTs plus 1 observational and 1 case report. Without a meta-analysis confirming agreement, the claim that thiamine reduces inflammation rests on narrative review and design heterogeneity. This is a weak inferential foundation.

concerns.issue: Very recent publication surge without long-term replication lag
concerns.detail: For all outcomes, a striking cluster of studies appeared in 2025–2026 (at minimum 15+ of the visible records). While recent evidence can be valid, this front-loading means there has been no opportunity for independent replication to occur, critical failures to be detected, or selective publication bias to be counterbalanced by null follow-up studies. The Wernicke encephalopathy and thiamine deficiency evidence spans 1993–2026, but cognition, cardiovascular, and inflammation are 2020–2026, limiting temporal robustness.

concerns.issue: Mechanism inferential gap for non-deficiency cognition/cardiovascular claims
concerns.detail: Strong evidence exists for thiamine's role in treating deficiency and Wernicke encephalopathy—clear, mechanistic conditions. But the claim that thiamine improves cognition in non-deficient populations or cardiovascular outcomes in heart failure (see 2019 RCT, 2020 RCT) requires a leap: from correction of enzymatic cofactor deficiency to enhancement of metabolism in replete individuals. The visible studies do not articulate a plausible dose–response or bioavailability mechanism that would support benefit in non-deficient states; the evidence base presented conflates treatment of deficiency with supplementation in sufficiency.

appraisal.mechanism_check: For thiamine deficiency and Wernicke encephalopathy, the mechanism is straightforward: thiamine is essential for pyruvate dehydrogenase, α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, and transketolase function; deficiency impairs energy metabolism and myelin synthesis, causing beriberi and neurologic damage. Repletion restores these functions. This mechanism directly supports the clinical outcomes. However, for cognition, cardiovascular, and inflammation in non-deficient populations, the records do not provide a mechanistic bridge. The studies treat thiamine as a general metabolic resuscitator or anti-inflammatory agent, but the evidence base does not clarify whether supraphysiologic thiamine enhances cofactor activity beyond saturation or operates via a distinct pathway. This is a substantial inferential leap not grounded in the submitted records.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would note that the strong-graded outcomes (deficiency, Wernicke) are treating a rare, easily reversible condition—severe deficiency—that naturally responds to any adequate thiamine supply. The more clinically relevant question is whether thiamine improves outcomes in populations with normal or marginal status (cardiac patients, critically ill, cognitively impaired non-alcoholic patients). For those populations, the evidence is Moderate, rests on single syntheses, lacks large RCTs, and omits sample sizes in most abstracts. A meta-analysis of n=298 in heart failure (2023) or an RCT of n=45 in pediatric cardiac function cannot rule out small effect size, publication bias, or placebo. If the true effect in non-deficient populations is negligible or confined to specific subgroups (e.g., alcoholics with marginal intake), the current Moderate grades overstate confidence.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: For cognition and cardiovascular outcomes: two or more independent, pre-registered, adequately powered RCTs (n ≥ 300 each) in non-deficient populations, with prespecified endpoints and open sample-size reporting, would resolve whether thiamine has a clinically meaningful effect beyond deficiency correction. For inflammation: a meta-analysis of human RCTs with explicit assessment of heterogeneity and funnel plot analysis would clarify whether apparent benefits are consistent or artifacts of small-study bias.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Vitamina B esencial que tu cuerpo utiliza para liberar energía de los alimentos; corrige enfermedades por deficiencia.
explanation_es.what_it_is: La tiamina, también llamada vitamina B1, es una vitamina soluble en agua que tus células necesitan para convertir alimentos (carbohidratos y ciertos aminoácidos) en energía utilizable. Tu cuerpo no puede fabricarla; debes obtenerla de alimentos o suplementos. Se encuentra naturalmente en granos integrales, cerdo, legumbres y nueces. Las personas típicamente la toman como tableta o cápsula oral, o la reciben por inyección—la forma inyectable se usa especialmente en contextos médicos para tratar o prevenir deficiencia grave.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Se convierte en una coenzima que permite que las enzimas liberen energía; apoya la función nerviosa y cardíaca.
explanation_es.how_it_works: La tiamina se convierte dentro de tus células en pirofosfato de tiamina (TPP), una molécula auxiliar (llamada coenzima) que funciona como una llave que encaja en una cerradura enzimática. Sin ella, varias enzimas críticas no pueden funcionar—específicamente aquellas que liberan energía de los carbohidratos y ayudan a construir y reparar el tejido nervioso y las membranas celulares. Por eso la deficiencia de tiamina daña primero el sistema nervioso y el corazón: esos tejidos dependen mucho de un suministro estable de energía. El TPP también juega un papel en manejar la señalización relacionada con la inflamación, aunque la imagen completa de cómo lo hace todavía está siendo investigada. Tu cerebro, corazón y músculos son especialmente sensibles a la escasez de tiamina porque queman energía constantemente.
explanation_es.safety_line: El uso oral e inyectado a corto plazo está bien tolerado; la seguridad a largo plazo e interacciones medicamentosas no han sido completamente estudiadas.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los ensayos recuperados reportan pocos eventos adversos en suplementación oral e intravenosa de tiamina a corto plazo, incluso con dosis altas. Sin embargo, la mayoría de estudios publicados incluyeron adultos durante días a semanas; la seguridad a largo plazo en la población general, efectos en niños fuera de contextos hospitalarios e interacciones con otros medicamentos no están bien caracterizados en los registros proporcionados.
safety_bullets: Embarazo y lactancia: la tiamina es esencial durante estos períodos, pero la dosificación óptima y seguridad de suplementación con dosis altas en personas embarazadas/lactantes no es abordada en los estudios recuperados.
Enfermedad renal y diálisis: algunos estudios recuperados incluyeron pacientes en diálisis, pero la seguridad de dosificación en insuficiencia renal grave permanece incompletamente definida.
Interacciones medicamentosas: ningún ensayo recuperado examinó interacciones de tiamina con clases mayores de fármacos; desconocidas en la práctica clínica.

Uso crónico con dosis altas: casi todos los estudios recuperados usaron suplementación durante días a semanas; los efectos de años de tiamina oral con dosis altas no están documentados en los registros proporcionados.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: La tiamina es una molécula polar, que ama el agua (XLogP 1 indica que se disuelve bien en agua y se absorbe del intestino delgado) con un anillo tiazolinio cargado positivamente. Esta carga y polaridad la hacen fácilmente absorbida oralmente pero también significan que no se acumula en tejido graso, así que el cuerpo excreta cantidades excesivas diariamente—la deficiencia puede desarrollarse rápidamente si la ingesta se corta.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Múltiples metanálisis y revisiones sistemáticas convergen en el hallazgo de que la suplementación con tiamina corrige y previene beriberi (una enfermedad que causa insuficiencia cardíaca, daño nervioso y muerte por deficiencia de tiamina). En estudios que incluyen más de 23.000 participantes verificados—incluyendo pacientes críticamente enfermos, pacientes en diálisis y poblaciones de alto riesgo de deficiencia—la administración de tiamina (oral e intravenosa, con varias dosis) revierte síntomas de deficiencia y reduce la mortalidad cuando la deficiencia está presente. Una revisión sistemática de 2024 de 688 personas examinó diagnóstico y tratamiento de encefalopatía de Wernicke (la forma neurológica aguda de deficiencia grave); un RCT de 2026 de 2.784 pacientes sépticos mostró que el uso de tiamina se asoció con reducción de mortalidad. La evidencia abarca años recientes (2021–2026) e incluye ensayos adecuadamente potenciados.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: El grado Fuerte refleja 52 estudios humanos con replicación independiente en 4 metanálisis, consistencia de dirección del efecto, y más de 23.000 participantes verificados en el resultado. La suplementación con tiamina para deficiencia establecida no es controversial—esta es práctica médica estándar respaldada por síntesis robusta.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: La suplementación con tiamina es efectiva para tratar y prevenir encefalopatía de Wernicke, una emergencia neurológica aguda (confusión, anomalías del movimiento ocular, ataxia—pérdida de coordinación) causada por deficiencia grave de tiamina. Una revisión sistemática de 2024 (n=688) examinó diagnóstico y tratamiento; un RCT de 2022 (n=393) investigó dosificación óptima de tiamina para prevenir y tratar síndrome de Wernicke–Korsakoff (la forma crónica). Más de 16.000 participantes verificados en 17 de 44 estudios demuestran que la administración rápida de tiamina, especialmente intravenosa, detiene la progresión e invierte síntomas tempranos. Tres metanálisis/revisiones sistemáticas independientes convergen en eficacia.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Grado Fuerte: 35 estudios humanos, 3 síntesis independientes confirmando resultado, aproximadamente 16.000 participantes verificados, y beneficio clínico claro en invertir una emergencia neurológica potencialmente mortal. La tiamina es el tratamiento de primera línea estándar para encefalopatía de Wernicke sospechada en medicina.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Un estudio piloto RCT de 2021 en pacientes de hemodiálisis con deterioro cognitivo, un RCT de 2021 (n=335) de suplementación con tiamina en bebés amamantados durante el primer año de vida, y un estudio observacional de 2022 (n=985) de pacientes hospitalizados con alteración del estado mental sugieren que la tiamina puede apoyar función cognitiva y recuperación del estado mental. Un RCT de 2022 (n=393) sobre dosificación óptima para encefalopatía de Wernicke también evaluó resultados cognitivos. Sin embargo, solo una metanálisis/revisión sistemática está documentada en los registros, y sus conclusiones no han sido replicadas independientemente.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Grado Moderado: 7 estudios humanos existen con alguna evidencia de beneficio cognitivo, pero solo una revisión de síntesis; sin replicación independiente de hallazgos agrupados. Los estudios abarcan diseños piloto y trabajo observacional, que son menos definitivos que múltiples RCTs grandes. El resultado es plausible—la tiamina es crítica para síntesis de neurotransmisores y metabolismo energético en el cerebro—pero la evidencia clínica permanece preliminar.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Un metanálisis de 2023 (n=298) examinó si la suplementación con tiamina afecta insuficiencia cardíaca; un RCT de 2020 investigó tiamina sostenida con dosis altas en pacientes cardíacos de alto riesgo sometidos a derivación cardiopulmonar; RCTs más antiguos (1997–1998) estudiaron efectos de tiamina en desempeño cardíaco y respuesta al ejercicio. Un informe de caso de 2026 describió mejora rápida en beriberi gastrointestinal (una emergencia relacionada con corazón) después de administración de tiamina. Aproximadamente 538 participantes verificados están documentados en 2 de 8 estudios; la mayoría de resúmenes carecen de tamaños de muestra, así que el total verdadero puede ser mayor. Sin embargo, solo un metanálisis aparece en los registros, y su conclusión no está verificada independientemente.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Grado Moderado: 6 estudios humanos con plausibilidad mecanística (la tiamina es esencial para producción de energía del músculo cardíaco) pero solo una síntesis y sin replicación independiente. Los estudios son pequeños a moderados en tamaño y abarcan décadas; RCTs recientes, grandes y adecuadamente potenciados específicamente en resultados cardíacos parecen limitados en los registros proporcionados. La evidencia para tiamina en enfermedad cardíaca establecida es sugestiva pero no definitiva.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Un RCT de 2022 (n=60) en diabetes gestacional encontró efectos anti-inflamatorios y antioxidantes de suplementos de tiamina; un RCT de 2022 (n=80) examinando combinación de vitamina C y tiamina en sepsis; un RCT de 2021 en pacientes con fatiga crónica; y un estudio observacional de 2026 (n=3.954) reportando una asociación en forma de L entre vitamina B1 y enfermedad inflamatoria pélvica. Los estudios en animales (n=300) mostraron que tiamina dietética mejoró actividad enzimática digestiva y desarrollo intestinal. Aproximadamente 4.394 participantes están verificados en 4 de 10 estudios; la mayoría de otros resúmenes omiten tamaño. Sin embargo, ningún análisis agrupado confirma que los múltiples estudios acuerden; la consistencia aún no está establecida.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Grado Moderado: 5 estudios humanos y 5 en animales sugieren potencial anti-inflamatorio, pero ningún metanálisis los ha sintetizado, y los estudios son algo heterogéneos en diseño y poblaciones (diabetes gestacional, sepsis, fatiga crónica, enfermedad pélvica). El papel mecanístico de la forma TPP de tiamina en señalización inflamatoria es plausible pero incompletamente entendido. La evidencia es sugestiva y justifica síntesis adicional pero queda corta de Fuerte.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La deficiencia de tiamina y encefalopatía de Wernicke tienen evidencia Fuerte (52 y 35 estudios humanos respectivamente, con múltiples metanálisis) y representan aplicaciones clínicas bien establecidas. Los resultados de cognición, cardiovascular e inflamación son grado Moderado y se basan en 5–7 estudios humanos por resultado con análisis agrupado limitado. La literatura está dominada por ensayos humanos (principalmente RCTs y revisiones sistemáticas de 2020–2026, con algo de trabajo más antiguo), reflejando décadas de uso clínico y enfoque renovado reciente en tiamina en enfermedad crítica y enfermedad neurológica. Los estudios en animales respaldan mecanismo pero son menos y no son la base de los grados clínicos.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros recuperados muestran evidencia fuerte para corrección de deficiencia y encefalopatía de Wernicke pero datos limitados sobre cognición, cardiovascular e inflamación en poblaciones con estado de tiamina normal o ligeramente deficiente—es incierto si la suplementación en personas con estado de tiamina normal confiere beneficio. La seguridad a largo plazo y dosificación óptima fuera de contextos hospitalarios agudos no están bien caracterizadas. Brechas específicas por resultado: estudios de cognición incluyen bebés y ancianos pero carecen de poblaciones de mediana edad; estudios cardiovasculares son pequeños y antiguos (excepto un ensayo de 2020); trabajo de inflamación abarca solo 5 ensayos humanos sin síntesis. Nota: estas brechas reflejan lo visible en los aproximadamente 40 resúmenes proporcionados por resultado; la literatura completa puede ser más amplia, pero no podemos evaluarla aquí.

appraisal_es.headline: La base de evidencia es genuinamente fuerte para deficiencia de tiamina y encefalopatía de Wernicke (con 4 metanálisis independientes y ~16k–24k participantes verificados), pero los resultados más débiles (cognición, cardiovascular, inflamación) se basan en síntesis únicas, estudios pequeños y diseños que frecuentemente omiten tamaños de muestra, limitando la confianza en esas afirmaciones.

concerns.issue: Reporte de tamaño de muestra opaco para resultados más débiles
concerns.detail: Para resultados de cognición, cardiovascular e inflamación, solo 5–38% de los estudios reportan tamaños de muestra en sus resúmenes. El motor señala 'la mayoría de resúmenes omiten el tamaño de muestra', lo que significa que la N verdadera es desconocida. Para cardiovascular, solo 2 de 8 estudios reportan N (298, 240); para inflamación, solo 4 de 10 lo reportan. Esta opacidad hace imposible evaluar si estos resultados se basan en precisión adecuada o son impulsados por un pequeño número de ensayos grandes—una distinción crítica para afirmaciones calificadas como Moderadas.

concerns.issue: Síntesis única solamente para cognición y cardiovascular
concerns.detail: Tanto los resultados de cognición como cardiovascular se califican como Moderados precisamente porque 'existe un único metanálisis / revisión sistemática, pero su conclusión no ha sido replicada o verificada de manera independiente.' Para cardiovascular, solo se enumera un metanálisis de 2023 (n=298). Si esa síntesis contiene sesgo o problemas metodológicos, no hay una segunda síntesis independiente para validarla o contradecirla. Esta es una limitación fundamental que el mismo motor identificó.

concerns.issue: Evidencia de inflamación carece de síntesis agrupada y confirmación de consistencia
concerns.detail: El motor señala explícitamente 'existen varios estudios pero ningún análisis agrupado confirma que estén de acuerdo; mantenido en moderado pendiente de revisión.' Los 10 estudios abarcan diseños animales y humanos; los 5 estudios humanos incluyen solo 3 ensayos controlados aleatorios más 1 observacional y 1 reporte de caso. Sin un metanálisis que confirme acuerdo, la afirmación de que la tiamina reduce la inflamación se basa en revisión narrativa y heterogeneidad de diseño. Esta es una base inferencial débil.

concerns.issue: Aumento muy reciente de publicaciones sin rezago de replicación a largo plazo
concerns.detail: Para todos los resultados, un cluster llamativo de estudios apareció en 2025–2026 (mínimo 15+ de los registros visibles). Aunque la evidencia reciente puede ser válida, este agrupamiento inicial significa que no ha habido oportunidad para que ocurra replicación independiente, se detecten fallas críticas, o se contrarreste el sesgo de publicación selectiva mediante estudios de seguimiento nulos. La evidencia de encefalopatía de Wernicke y deficiencia de tiamina abarca 1993–2026, pero cognición, cardiovascular e inflamación son 2020–2026, limitando la robustez temporal.

concerns.issue: Brecha inferencial de mecanismo para afirmaciones de cognición/cardiovascular sin deficiencia
concerns.detail: Existe evidencia fuerte del papel de la tiamina en tratar deficiencia y encefalopatía de Wernicke—condiciones claras y mecanísticas. Pero la afirmación de que la tiamina mejora la cognición en poblaciones no deficientes o resultados cardiovasculares en insuficiencia cardíaca (ver ensayos RCT de 2019, 2020) requiere un salto: de corrección de deficiencia del cofactor enzimático a mejora del metabolismo en individuos repletos. Los estudios visibles no articulan un mecanismo plausible de relación dosis-respuesta o biodisponibilidad que apoye beneficio en estados no deficientes; la base de evidencia presentada conflate tratamiento de deficiencia con suplementación en suficiencia.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: Para deficiencia de tiamina y encefalopatía de Wernicke, el mecanismo es directo: la tiamina es esencial para función de piruvato deshidrogenasa, α-cetoglutarato deshidrogenasa y transketolasa; la deficiencia afecta el metabolismo energético y síntesis de mielina, causando beriberi y daño neurológico. La repleción restaura estas funciones. Este mecanismo respalda directamente los resultados clínicos. Sin embargo, para cognición, cardiovascular e inflamación en poblaciones no deficientes, los registros no proporcionan un puente mecanístico. Los estudios tratan la tiamina como un resuscitador metabólico general o agente antiinflamatorio, pero la base de evidencia no aclara si la tiamina suprafisiológica mejora la actividad del cofactor más allá de saturación u opera a través de una vía distinta. Este es un salto inferencial sustancial no fundamentado en los registros presentados.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico señalaría que los resultados calificados como fuertes (deficiencia, Wernicke) están tratando una condición rara, fácilmente reversible—deficiencia severa—que responde naturalmente a cualquier aporte adecuado de tiamina. La pregunta más clínicamente relevante es si la tiamina mejora resultados en poblaciones con estatus normal o marginal (pacientes cardíacos, críticamente enfermos, pacientes con discapacidad cognitiva no alcohólicos). Para esas poblaciones, la evidencia es Moderada, se basa en síntesis únicas, carece de grandes ensayos RCT, y omite tamaños de muestra en la mayoría de resúmenes. Un metanálisis de n=298 en insuficiencia cardíaca (2023) o un RCT de n=45 en función cardíaca pediátrica no pueden descartar tamaño de efecto pequeño, sesgo de publicación, o placebo. Si el efecto verdadero en poblaciones no deficientes es negligible o está confinado a subgrupos específicos (p. ej., alcohólicos con ingesta marginal), las calificaciones Moderadas actuales sobrestiman la confianza.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Para resultados de cognición y cardiovascular: dos o más ensayos RCT independientes, preregistrados, adecuadamente potenciados (n ≥ 300 cada uno) en poblaciones no deficientes, con endpoints prespecificados y reporte de tamaño de muestra abierto, resolverían si la tiamina tiene un efecto clínicamente significativo más allá de corrección de deficiencia. Para inflamación: un metanálisis de RCT humanos con evaluación explícita de heterogeneidad y análisis de gráfico de embudo aclararía si los beneficios aparentes son consistentes o artefactos de sesgo de estudios pequeños.
